boundaries.deterministic: bytes in, bytes out: every conforming implementation gives the same answer for every input
boundaries.proven: deterministic, and a machine-checked proof covers the stated property
boundaries.vector-tested: held only by the vectors here; agreement outside them is not claimed
boundaries.heuristic: no agreement is promised; only the stated bounds

blob-hash.what: SHA-256 over raw bytes, no framing
blob-hash.bite_proof: positive-only class: a wrong digest fails every vector

canon.what: RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical bytes of a warrant body, and their SHA-256 (the WarrantID)
canon.bite_proof: warrant tests/canon_*; UTF-16 key ordering and number forms are vectored
canon.limit: inputs are warrant bodies: a generic JCS (floats, deep nesting) is not covered

sig-message.what: the 47 bytes a warrant signature covers: "warrant-sig-v1:" || WarrantID_raw
sig-message.bite_proof: positive-only class; wrong constructions are verify-sig negatives

verify-sig.what: Ed25519 (cofactorless, small-order and non-canonical keys rejected) and, with alg, ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 (compressed key, 64-byte r||s, low-S)

p256-decode.what: a compressed SEC1 P-256 key decoded alone: the point, or a refusal
p256-decode.spec: SEC 1 v2 §2.3.4, narrowed by warrant WRT-019 (compressed, lowercase, x < p, on the curve)

proofs.covers: the hex layer only: hexcanon::decode accepts exactly the lowercase spellings encode writes (complete and canonical); the curve checks after it are vector-tested, not proved
proofs.bite_proof: proofs/creusot/mutants.py: 5/5 mutants make the proof fail
